mutual informations; monogamy statements forcing a wormhole to have exactly two mouths;
weak duality for bit-thread flows, saturated for the elementary wormhole (max-flow $=$
min-cut for a single bridge); a functorial coarse-graining that widens throats,
contracts the emergent metric $1$-Lipschitzly and is strict in general; and a complete
computation of the emergent geometry of $n$ Bell pairs.
\end{abstract}

\maketitle

\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The idea}
Two ideas from the last two decades of quantum gravity sit at the heart of this paper. The
first is the \emph{Ryu--Takayanagi prescription}: in a holographic system, the entanglement
entropy of a boundary region equals the area of the minimal bulk surface anchored to its
edge. Entropy, an information-theoretic quantity, is measured by a geometric one. The
second is \emph{ER $=$ EPR}: the proposal that an entangled pair of particles is connected
by a microscopic Einstein--Rosen bridge, so that spacetime connectivity is a consequence of
entanglement rather than a separate ingredient of physics. Van Raamsdonk's thought
experiment sharpens the second: disentangle two halves of a holographic state and the bulk
pinches off; in the limit, space itself is torn in two.

Both statements are, natively, statements about continuous manifolds, quantum field
theories and an incompletely understood duality. This paper asks a narrower question with a
complete answer: \emph{in the simplest combinatorial model that supports a Ryu--Takayanagi
prescription, what exactly does ER $=$ EPR say, and is it true?} The answer is that it says a
great deal, and all of it is true --- with a caveat and a sharp constant at each step.

\subsection{Contributions}
The min-cut model of holographic entropy is classical: subadditivity, strong subadditivity,
monogamy of mutual information and purity all follow from surface recombination. Our
contribution is to move past entropy inequalities into geometry. We introduce the throat
capacity as an observable in its own right and prove it detects connectivity exactly
(\S\ref{sec:throat}); we prove the toy-model cross-section inequality $I \le 2E$ with a
sharp constant, from a four-variable Boolean lemma (\S\ref{sec:cross}); we show the
resulting distance function is an ultrametric, hence $0$-hyperbolic, and reconstructible
from two-point entanglement data alone (\S\ref{sec:tree}); we prove monogamy statements
forcing the wormhole network to be a tree (\S\ref{sec:monogamy}); we introduce flows and
prove weak duality against throat capacity with a matching flow for the elementary
wormhole (\S\ref{sec:threads}); we construct a functorial coarse-graining operation and
prove it is a strict metric contraction (\S\ref{sec:rg}); and we compute the emergent
geometry of $n$ Bell pairs completely (\S\ref{sec:bell}). Everything is stated for finite
models with real, nonnegative, symmetric areas; no continuum limit and no unproved duality
is used.

\section{The model}

Fix a finite set $V$ of \emph{cells} --- the discrete spatial slice.

\begin{definition}[Geometry]
A \emph{geometry} on $V$ is a map $w : V\times V \to \R$ with $w(x,y)=w(y,x)$ and
$w(x,y)\ge 0$. We read $w(x,y)$ as the area of the elementary surface element separating
cell $x$ from cell $y$; $w(x,y)=0$ means the two cells are not adjacent.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Region and area]
A \emph{region} is a Boolean function $f : V \to \{\true,\false\}$, identified with the set
$\{x : f(x)=\true\}$. Its \emph{area} is
\[
\area(f) \;=\; \tfrac12 \sum_{x\in V}\sum_{y \in V} [\,f(x)\ne f(y)\,]\,w(x,y),
\]
where $[\,\cdot\,]$ is $1$ if the condition holds and $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One-sided forms of the area]\label{lem:onesided}
For every region $f$,
\[
\area(f) \;=\; \sum_{x}\sum_{y}\,[\,f(x)=\true \text{ and } f(y)=\false\,]\,w(x,y)
\;=\; \sum_{f(x)=\true}\ \sum_{f(y)=\false} w(x,y).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For each ordered pair $(x,y)$ the summand $[f(x)\ne f(y)]w(x,y)$ splits as
$[f(x)=\true,f(y)=\false]w(x,y)+[f(y)=\true,f(x)=\false]w(x,y)$, a four-case check.
Swapping indices in the second term and using symmetry of $w$ shows the two double sums
agree, so each equals half the original.
\end{proof}

The area function satisfies $\area(f)=\area(\neg f)$ and is \emph{submodular},
\[
\area(f\wedge g)+\area(f\vee g)\;\le\;\area(f)+\area(g),
\]
both by pointwise inequalities on the Boolean separation indicator. Cells $x,y$ are
\emph{adjacent} when $w(x,y)>0$; a \emph{bulk path} from $u$ to $v$ is a finite chain of
consecutively adjacent cells, written $u \rw v$.

\begin{definition}[Holographic model]
A \emph{holographic model} is a geometry $w$ on $V$ together with a set
$\partial V \subseteq V$ of \emph{boundary cells}. Cells outside $\partial V$ are
\emph{hidden bulk cells}; a model has \emph{no hidden bulk} if $\partial V = V$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Admissibility and entropy]
A region $f$ is \emph{admissible} for a boundary region $A$ if $f(v)=A(v)$ for every
$v \in \partial V$; hidden cells are unconstrained. The \emph{entropy} of $A$ is
$S(A)=\min\{\area(f) : f \text{ admissible for } A\}$, attained since the family is finite
and nonempty. A minimiser is a \emph{minimal surface} for $A$.
\end{definition}

This is the discrete Ryu--Takayanagi prescription; the requirement that $f$ agree with $A$
on the boundary is the homology constraint.

\begin{definition}[Mutual information]
For disjoint boundary regions, $I(A:B)=S(A)+S(B)-S(A\cup B)$.
\end{definition}

Submodularity gives $I \ge 0$ at once, and the standard recombination arguments give strong
subadditivity and monogamy of mutual information. We record one further inequality.

\begin{theorem}[Araki--Lieb]
For disjoint boundary regions $A,B$ we have $S(A)\le S(A\cup B)+S(B)$, and hence
$|S(A)-S(B)| \le S(A\cup B)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Entropy is \emph{pure}: $S(X)=S(\partial V\setminus X)$, because a region and its
complement bound the same surface. Let $C$ be the boundary complement of $A\cup B$; on the
boundary the complement of $A$ is $C\cup B$, so $S(A)=S(C\cup B)\le S(C)+S(B)$ by
subadditivity, and $S(C)=S(A\cup B)$ by purity. Exchanging $A$ and $B$ gives the two-sided
form.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Star area]\label{lem:star}
For any geometry and cell $u$, $\area(\{u\}) = \sum_{y\ne u} w(u,y)$.
\end{lemma}

Consequently, in a model with no hidden bulk, $S(\{u\})=\sum_{y\ne u}w(u,y)$ and
$I(u:v)=2w(u,v)$: the mutual information of two cells is twice the area of the edge joining
them.

\begin{example}[The elementary wormhole]\label{ex:pair}
Let $V=\{0,1\}$, both cells on the boundary, $w(0,1)=w\ge 0$. Then
$S(\{0\})=S(\{1\})=w$, $S(\{0,1\})=0$ and $I(0:1)=2w$. This \emph{pair model} is the
smallest Einstein--Rosen bridge and saturates every inequality below.
\end{example}

\section{Throat capacity: the width of a bridge}\label{sec:throat}

\begin{definition}[Separating surface; throat capacity]
A region $\sigma$ \emph{separates} $A$ from $B$ if $A \subseteq \sigma$ and
$B\cap\sigma=\emptyset$. The \emph{throat capacity} is
\[
E(A,B)=\min\{\area(\sigma) : \sigma \text{ separates } A \text{ from } B\},
\]
set to $0$ when no separating region exists. For disjoint $A,B$ the family is nonempty
($\sigma=A$), so the minimum is attained.
\end{definition}

$E(A,B)$ is the cross-section of the Einstein--Rosen bridge joining $A$ to $B$: the
discrete analogue of the entanglement wedge cross-section $E_W$. Unlike entropy, it
minimises over \emph{all} separating regions, not only those homologous to a boundary
region.

\begin{proposition}
$E(A,B)\ge 0$; $E(A,B)=E(B,A)$; and $E$ is monotone in the geometry: $w \le w'$ pointwise
implies $E_w(A,B)\le E_{w'}(A,B)$ for disjoint $A,B$. Symmetry holds because complementing
a minimal $A$--$B$ separating surface gives a $B$--$A$ separating surface of equal area.
\end{proposition}

Monotonicity is already a form of Van Raamsdonk's principle: more entanglement means a
wider bridge.

\begin{lemma}[Zero area means closed]\label{lem:zeroclosed}
$\area(\sigma)=0$ if and only if $w(x,y)=0$ for all $x$ with $\sigma(x)=\true$ and $y$ with
$\sigma(y)=\false$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:onesided} the area is a sum of nonnegative terms over crossing pairs, and
such a sum vanishes iff every term does.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Closed regions absorb paths]\label{lem:absorb}
If $\sigma$ is closed in the sense of Lemma~\ref{lem:zeroclosed}, $u\rw v$ and
$\sigma(u)=\true$, then $\sigma(v)=\true$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Bridge detection]\label{thm:detect}
For $u \ne v$: $\;E(u,v)>0 \iff u \rw v$. Bulk connectivity is decided by a single real
number.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
If no path joins $u$ to $v$, the reachable set $R=\{x : u \rw x\}$ contains $u$, misses
$v$, and admits no positive-weight step out of it; so $R$ separates $u$ from $v$ and
$\area(R)=0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:zeroclosed}, forcing $E(u,v)=0$. Conversely if $E(u,v)=0$,
a minimal separating surface has zero area, hence is closed, hence by
Lemma~\ref{lem:absorb} traps every path from $u$ on $u$'s side, while $v$ lies on the other
side.
\end{proof}

\section{Entanglement is bounded by the cross-section}\label{sec:cross}

\begin{lemma}[Splitting inequality]\label{lem:split}
For all bits $a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2$,
\[
[\,a_1\wedge b_1 \ne a_2 \wedge b_2\,] + [\,\neg a_1 \wedge b_1 \ne \neg a_2 \wedge b_2\,]
\;\le\; [\,b_1\ne b_2\,] + 2\,[\,a_1 \ne a_2\,],
\]
and the constant $2$ is sharp: for $a_1=\true$, $a_2=\false$, $b_1=b_2=\true$ both sides
equal $2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Sixteen cases. If $a_1=a_2$ the right side is $[b_1\ne b_2]$ and the left side is at most
that, since conjunction with a common bit can only merge values. If $a_1 \ne a_2$ the right
side is at least $2$, which dominates the left side.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Area splitting]\label{prop:areasplit}
For all regions $\sigma, g$,
$\area(\sigma\wedge g)+\area(\neg\sigma\wedge g) \le \area(g)+2\area(\sigma)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:split} pointwise with $a_i=\sigma(x_i)$, $b_i=g(x_i)$, multiply by
$w(x,y)\ge 0$, and sum.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Cross-section bound]\label{thm:cross}
For disjoint boundary regions $A$ and $B$, $\;I(A:B) \le 2\,E(A,B)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Pick $\sigma$ realising $E(A,B)$ and a minimal surface $g$ for $A\cup B$. On a boundary
cell, $g=A\vee B$, while $\sigma$ contains $A$ and misses $B$; a three-case check gives
$(\sigma\wedge g)|_{\partial V}=A$ and $(\neg\sigma\wedge g)|_{\partial V}=B$, so both are
admissible. Hence
\[
S(A)+S(B) \le \area(\sigma\wedge g)+\area(\neg\sigma\wedge g)
\le \area(g)+2\area(\sigma) = S(A\cup B)+2E(A,B)
\]
by Proposition~\ref{prop:areasplit}. Rearranging is the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The ER $=$ EPR sandwich]\label{thm:sandwich}
For disjoint boundary regions,
\[
\tfrac12 I(A:B) \;\le\; E(A,B) \;\le\; \min\bigl(S(A),S(B)\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The left inequality is Theorem~\ref{thm:cross}. For the right, a minimal surface $f$ for
$A$ agrees with $A$ on the boundary, hence contains $A$ and misses the disjoint boundary
region $B$; so $f$ separates them and $E(A,B)\le\area(f)=S(A)$. Symmetry of $E$ gives the
same with $B$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[ER $=$ EPR, quantitative form]
Let $u\ne v$ be boundary cells with $I(u:v)>0$. Then $E(u,v)\ge\tfrac12 I(u:v)>0$, and
consequently $u \rw v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharpness]\label{thm:sharp}
In the elementary wormhole of Example~\ref{ex:pair}, $E(0,1)=w$ and $I(0:1)=2w=2E(0,1)$;
in Theorem~\ref{thm:sandwich} all three quantities equal $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The region $\{0\}$ separates $0$ from $1$ with area $w$, so $E \le w$; and
$E \ge \tfrac12 I = w$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:cross}.
\end{proof}

\section{Emergent spacetime is a tree}\label{sec:tree}

\begin{definition}
For cells $u,v$ set $\cpc(u,v)=E(\{u\},\{v\})$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Gomory--Hu inequality]\label{thm:gh}
For $u \ne w$ and any third cell $v$, $\;\min(\cpc(u,v),\cpc(v,w)) \le \cpc(u,w)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Let $\sigma$ realise $\cpc(u,w)$. The cell $v$ lies on one of its two sides. If
$\sigma(v)=\true$ then $\sigma$ separates $v$ from $w$; if $\sigma(v)=\false$ then $\sigma$
separates $u$ from $v$. Either way one of the two capacities is at most $\area(\sigma)$.
\end{proof}

The hypothesis $u \ne w$ is essential, since $\cpc(u,u)=0$: no surface separates a cell
from itself.

\begin{definition}[Emergent distance]
$d(u,v)=0$ if $u=v$ and $d(u,v)=e^{-\cpc(u,v)}$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Emergent spacetime is an ultrametric space]\label{thm:ultra}
$d$ is a metric on $V$ with $0 \le d \le 1$, and it satisfies the strong triangle
inequality
\[
d(u,w) \;\le\; \max\bigl(d(u,v),\,d(v,w)\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Nonnegativity, symmetry and $d(u,v)=0 \iff u=v$ are immediate since $e^{-t}>0$. For the
strong triangle inequality the degenerate cases are trivial; otherwise apply the
order-reversing map $t\mapsto e^{-t}$ to Theorem~\ref{thm:gh}, which turns the minimum of
capacities into the maximum of distances and reverses the inequality. The ordinary triangle
inequality follows since $\max(a,b)\le a+b$ for $a,b\ge 0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Ultrametricity is strictly stronger than the triangle inequality and is the hallmark of
tree-like geometry. The exponential is used only for being order-reversing, but it has two
extra virtues: it normalises ``no bridge'' to distance exactly $1$, and it converts the
additive bound $I\le 2E$ into the multiplicative Theorem~\ref{thm:vanR}.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Zero hyperbolicity]
Every ultrametric space satisfies Gromov's four-point condition with $\delta=0$:
\[
d(x,y)+d(z,t) \;\le\; \max\bigl(d(x,z)+d(y,t),\; d(x,t)+d(y,z)\bigr).
\]
In particular the emergent spacetime of any geometry is $0$-hyperbolic.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Suppose both terms on the right are strictly smaller than the left. Apply the strong
triangle inequality four times: to $d(x,y)$ through $z$ and through $t$, and to $d(z,t)$
through $x$ and through $y$. Each offers two alternatives; the assumed strict inequalities
eliminate one in each branch, and the surviving four bounds combine linearly into
$d(x,y)+d(z,t) < d(x,y)+d(z,t)$, a contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Disentangling tears space apart]\label{thm:tear}
For $u \ne v$: $d(u,v)=1$ iff no bridge joins $u$ to $v$, and $d(u,v)<1$ iff $u \rw v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distance decays exponentially in entanglement]\label{thm:vanR}
For distinct boundary cells, $\;d(u,v) \le e^{-I(u:v)/2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity]
If $w \le w'$ pointwise then $d_{w'} \le d_w$ pointwise: adding entanglement can only bring
the emergent spacetime closer together.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{A hierarchy of scales}

\begin{theorem}[Entanglement clusters at every scale]
For each $r \ge 0$ the relation $u \sim_r v :\iff d(u,v)\le r$ is an equivalence relation
on $V$, and the induced partitions are monotone: $r \le s$ implies $\sim_r$ refines
$\sim_s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Reflexivity and symmetry are clear; transitivity is exactly the strong triangle inequality,
$d(u,w)\le\max(d(u,v),d(v,w))\le r$. Transitivity is false for a general metric --- this is
a purely ultrametric phenomenon.
\end{proof}

Two unconnected cells stay in different clusters at every scale $r<1$, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:tear}.

\subsection{Reconstruction}

\begin{theorem}[The emergent metric is a function of the entanglement data]
Let $M,N$ be holographic models on the same cell set, both without hidden bulk cells, with
$I_M(u:v)=I_N(u:v)$ for all $u,v$. Then $d_M = d_N$, and the identity map is an isometry of
the emergent metric spaces. In particular the emergent metric space --- with its
ultrametric structure, its $0$-hyperbolicity and its full hierarchy of clusters --- is an
invariant of the entanglement structure alone.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Without hidden bulk, $I(u:v)=2w(u,v)$ for $u \ne v$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:star}), so equality of
mutual informations forces equality of all off-diagonal weights. Areas do not see the
diagonal, so all cut weights agree, hence the minima defining $\cpc$ agree, hence $d$
agrees.
\end{proof}

\section{Monogamy: a wormhole has two mouths}\label{sec:monogamy}

\begin{theorem}[The wormhole network is a tree]
Let $u,v,w$ be cells with $u \ne w$, $v\ne w$. If $\cpc(u,w)<\cpc(u,v)$ then
$\cpc(u,w)=\cpc(v,w)$. Equivalently: of the three capacities of a triple, the two smallest
are always equal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:gh} twice, as $\min(\cpc(u,v),\cpc(v,w))\le\cpc(u,w)$ and
$\min(\cpc(u,v),\cpc(u,w))\le\cpc(v,w)$. The hypothesis makes the first minimum
$\cpc(v,w)$, giving $\cpc(v,w)\le\cpc(u,w)$, and the second minimum $\cpc(u,w)$, giving the
reverse inequality.
\end{proof}

This isosceles law characterises leaf metrics of weighted trees.

\begin{theorem}[Monogamy of Einstein--Rosen bridges]
Let $M$ be a holographic model without hidden bulk cells and $u \ne v$ cells with
$I(u:v)=2S(\{u\})$. Then for every cell $z \notin \{u,v\}$ we have $w(u,z)=0$ and
$I(u:z)=0$: the cell $u$ has no bridge other than the one to $v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Without hidden bulk, $S(\{u\})=\sum_{y\ne u}w(u,y)$ and $I(u:v)=2w(u,v)$, so saturation
reads $\sum_{y\ne u,v}w(u,y)=0$. All weights are nonnegative, so every term vanishes;
$w(u,z)=0$ and then $I(u:z)=2w(u,z)=0$.
\end{proof}

Positivity of areas is precisely where physics enters. The no-hidden-bulk hypothesis is not
cosmetic: with hidden cells $S(\{u\})$ is a genuine min-cut, possibly strictly smaller than
the sum of incident weights, and saturation no longer forces the edges to vanish.

\begin{corollary}[Geometric monogamy]
Under the same hypotheses, $v$ is the unique neighbour of $u$ in the emergent geometry.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{The lattice of minimal surfaces and wedge nesting}

\begin{theorem}[Minimal surfaces form a lattice]
If $f$ and $g$ are both minimal surfaces for the same boundary region $A$, so are
$f\wedge g$ and $f \vee g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Both are admissible for $A$, so both areas are $\ge S(A)$; submodularity bounds their sum
by $2S(A)$. Two numbers each at least $S(A)$ and summing to at most $2S(A)$ both equal
$S(A)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Entanglement wedge nesting]
If $A \subseteq B$ are boundary regions, one may choose minimal surfaces $f$ for $A$ and
$g$ for $B$ with $f \subseteq g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Given arbitrary minimal $f_0, g_0$, containment on the boundary makes $f_0 \wedge g_0$
admissible for $A$ and $f_0\vee g_0$ admissible for $B$; submodularity forces both to be
minimal, and $f_0\wedge g_0 \subseteq f_0\vee g_0$.
\end{proof}

\section{Bit threads: flowing through the bridge}\label{sec:threads}

\begin{definition}[Bit thread configuration]
A \emph{bit thread configuration} on a geometry $w$ is $\phi : V\times V \to \R$ that is
antisymmetric, $\phi(x,y)=-\phi(y,x)$, and capacity-respecting, $\phi(x,y)\le w(x,y)$.
Since $w$ is symmetric, antisymmetry upgrades the one-sided bound to
$|\phi(x,y)|\le w(x,y)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}
The \emph{divergence} is $\dvg\phi(x)=\sum_y \phi(x,y)$. The configuration is
\emph{conserved} relative to $(A,B)$ if $\dvg\phi(v)=0$ for every $v \notin A\cup B$. Its
\emph{value} is $\val(\phi)=\sum_{x\in A}\dvg\phi(x)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Antisymmetric kernels vanish on squares]\label{lem:antisum}
If $\phi$ is antisymmetric then $\sum_{x\in S}\sum_{y\in S}\phi(x,y)=0$ for every
$S \subseteq V$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Weak duality]\label{thm:weakdual}
Let $\phi$ be conserved relative to $(A,B)$ and let $\sigma$ be any region separating $A$
from $B$. Then $\val(\phi)\le \area(\sigma)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Three steps. (i) Every cell of $\sigma$ outside $A$ is also outside $B$, so its divergence
vanishes by conservation and $\val(\phi)=\sum_{x\in\sigma}\dvg\phi(x)$. (ii) Split each
divergence over $\sigma$ and its complement; the double sum inside $\sigma$ vanishes by
Lemma~\ref{lem:antisum}, leaving $\sum_{x\in\sigma}\sum_{y\notin\sigma}\phi(x,y)$. (iii)
Termwise $\phi(x,y)\le w(x,y)$, and the resulting double sum is exactly $\area(\sigma)$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:onesided}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
For disjoint $A,B$, every conserved configuration satisfies $\val(\phi)\le E(A,B)$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Max-flow $=$ min-cut for a single Einstein--Rosen bridge]
In the elementary wormhole of weight $w$, the configuration $\phi(0,1)=w$,
$\phi(1,0)=-w$, $\phi(x,x)=0$ is a conserved bit thread configuration with source $\{0\}$
and sink $\{1\}$, and
\[
\val(\phi)=w=E(0,1)=\tfrac12 I(0:1),
\]
and no conserved configuration has larger value.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Antisymmetry and capacity are immediate; conservation is vacuous. The value is
$\dvg\phi(0)=w$. Optimality is weak duality together with $E(0,1)=w$ from
Theorem~\ref{thm:sharp}.
\end{proof}

The general converse --- a saturating flow for every geometry and every pair of regions ---
is a max-flow--min-cut theorem, stated as Conjecture~\ref{conj:C1}. Note that the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:weakdual} uses neither finiteness beyond summability nor symmetry of the
weights except through Lemma~\ref{lem:onesided}.

\section{A renormalisation flow on emergent spacetime}\label{sec:rg}

\begin{definition}[Pushforward geometry]
For a map $\pi : V \to W$ of finite cell sets, the \emph{pushforward} of a geometry $w$ is
\[
(\pi_* w)(a,b) = \begin{cases} 0, & a=b, \\
\displaystyle\sum_{x\in\pi^{-1}(a)}\sum_{y\in\pi^{-1}(b)} w(x,y), & a \ne b. \end{cases}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Coarse surfaces are invariant fine surfaces of equal area]\label{thm:push}
For every region $\sigma$ of $W$, $\;\area_{\pi_*w}(\sigma)=\area_w(\sigma\circ\pi)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Expand both sides and group the fine sum by fibres. The diagonal correction $a=b$ costs
nothing because $\sigma\circ\pi$ is constant on a fibre, so the separation indicator
vanishes there anyway.
\end{proof}

This says every coarse surface pulls back to a fine surface of the same area, but not
conversely: fine surfaces that \emph{split a fibre} have no coarse counterpart. The whole
renormalisation flow is this asymmetry.

\begin{theorem}[Functoriality]
For $\pi : V\to W$ and $\rho : W \to X$, $\;\rho_*(\pi_* w) = (\rho\circ\pi)_* w$ as
geometries.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Regroup fibres of $\pi$ inside fibres of $\rho$. For $c\ne d$ the fibres $\rho^{-1}(c)$ and
$\rho^{-1}(d)$ are disjoint, so the diagonal correction is never triggered --- which is why
the composite is an equality rather than an inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Coarse-graining widens throats]
For disjoint coarse regions $A,B$,
$\;E_w(A\circ\pi,\,B\circ\pi) \le E_{\pi_*w}(A,B)$; in particular
$\cpc_w(u,v)\le\cpc_{\pi_*w}(\pi u,\pi v)$ whenever $\pi u \ne \pi v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
A minimal coarse separating surface pulls back, by Theorem~\ref{thm:push}, to a fine
separating surface of the same area; the fine minimisation ranges over a larger family.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Coarse-graining is a metric contraction]
$d_{\pi_*w}(\pi u, \pi v) \le d_w(u,v)$ for all $u,v$; i.e.\ $\pi$ is $1$-Lipschitz from
the emergent ultrametric space of $w$ to that of $\pi_* w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coarse-graining cannot decrease entropy]
If a coarse cell is a boundary cell as soon as one of the cells it absorbs is, then
$S_w(A\circ\pi) \le S_{\pi_*w}(A)$ for every coarse boundary region $A$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity]
If some minimal $u$--$v$ separating surface of $w$ is constant on the fibres of $\pi$ ---
i.e.\ is pulled back from a coarse surface $\tau$ with $\tau(\pi u)=\true$,
$\tau(\pi v)=\false$ --- then $\cpc_{\pi_*w}(\pi u,\pi v)=\cpc_w(u,v)$. The analogous
statement holds for entropies.
\end{theorem}

Together with the next theorem, this isolates the exact mechanism of the renormalisation
jump: only surfaces that split a fibre can be lost.

\begin{theorem}[The contraction is strict]
Consider four cells in a path $0-1-2-3$ with $w(0,1)=5$, $w(1,2)=1$, $w(2,3)=5$ and all
other weights $0$, and let $\pi$ merge the waist cells $1$ and $2$. Then
$\cpc_w(0,3)\le 1$ while $\cpc_{\pi_*w}(\pi 0,\pi 3)=5$, so
$d_{\pi_*w}(\pi 0,\pi 3) < d_w(0,3)$ strictly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Upper bound: the region $\{0,1\}$ separates $0$ from $3$ and its bounding surface is the
single waist edge, of area $1$. After merging, the coarse geometry is a three-cell path
with both edges of area $5$ (the waist becomes internal, hence invisible), so every coarse
surface separating the ends cuts exactly one heavy edge; exhausting the two positions of
the middle cell gives the exact value $5$.
\end{proof}

\section{Worked example: the emergent space of $n$ Bell pairs}\label{sec:bell}

Let $V=\{1,\dots,n\}\times\{0,1\}$, all cells on the boundary, with
$w((i,b),(j,c)) = w_i \ge 0$ if $i=j$ and $b\ne c$, and $0$ otherwise.

\begin{theorem}
For all $i,j,b,c$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\area(\{(i,b)\}) = w_i$;
\item $\cpc((i,b),(i,\bar b)) = w_i$;
\item $\cpc((i,b),(j,c)) = 0$ for $i \ne j$;
\item $d((i,b),(i,\bar b)) = e^{-w_i}$ and $d((i,b),(j,c))=1$ for $i \ne j$;
\item $w_i>0$ if and only if the two mouths of pair $i$ are at distance strictly less
than $1$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(1) is Lemma~\ref{lem:star}: only the partner edge is nonzero. (2) has an upper bound from
the surface around a single cell and a lower bound for free from Theorem~\ref{thm:cross}
applied to $I=2w_i$. (3) holds because no bulk path leaves a pair, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:detect} forces the capacity to vanish. (4) and (5) are immediate.
\end{proof}

This is the sharpest instance of the sandwich: all three of $\tfrac12 I$, $E$ and
$\min(S,S)$ equal $w_i$.

\begin{theorem}[The clusters are exactly the Bell pairs]
Let $\max_i e^{-w_i} \le r < 1$. Then two cells lie in the same cluster of the emergent
ultrametric at scale $r$ if and only if they belong to the same Bell pair.
\end{theorem}

Both hypotheses on $r$ are needed: without $r<1$ distinct pairs would merge, and without
$e^{-w_i}\le r$ a pair with a thin throat would already be split.

\section{Discussion}

\subsection{What the model shows}
Read as one statement: given the two-point entanglement data of a holographic state with no
hidden bulk, one reconstructs a metric space; that space is ultrametric, hence
$0$-hyperbolic; distances decay exponentially in mutual information; positive mutual
information is equivalent to bulk connectivity; the bridge cross-section is sandwiched
between half the mutual information and the entropies of the mouths, with equality for a
single throat; maximal entanglement forces a bridge with exactly two mouths; entanglement is
transportable through the bridge as a conserved flow whose maximal value is at most the
cross-section, with equality for a single throat; and coarse-graining contracts this
geometry $1$-Lipschitzly and functorially, strictly so whenever it absorbs the surfaces
carrying the min-cut.

That is a considerable amount of ER $=$ EPR made precise and true. It is also a toy: no
dynamics, no time, no Einstein equations, and areas that are combinatorial inputs rather
than solutions of anything. What it isolates is the purely kinematic content of the
correspondence --- the part following from the min-cut structure alone. That this part
already yields negative curvature, monogamy, a renormalisation flow and a reconstruction
theorem is the interesting news.

\subsection{Algorithms}
All quantities here are computable. For $|V|=n$: areas cost $O(n^2)$; throat capacity is an
undirected minimum $s$--$t$ cut, computable in polynomial time by max-flow; entropy is a
min-cut with boundary values fixed, i.e.\ an $s$--$t$ min-cut after contracting $A$ to a
source and its boundary complement to a sink, hidden cells free; the full capacity table
costs $\binom n2$ min-cuts naively, or $n-1$ via a Gomory--Hu tree, whose existence is
guaranteed by Theorem~\ref{thm:gh}; the cluster hierarchy is single-linkage clustering on
the capacity table; and bit threads are a maximum flow, with weak duality supplying the
certificate.

\subsection{Future directions}

\begin{conjecture}[Strong duality]\label{conj:C1}
For every finite geometry and disjoint boundary regions $A,B$ there exists a conserved
thread configuration $T$ with $\val(T)=E(A,B)$; consequently max-flow $=$ min-cut, and the
Ryu--Takayanagi entropy of any region is the maximal flux of a bit-thread configuration out
of it.
\end{conjecture}
The weak duality proved here uses only antisymmetry plus capacity, so the missing half is
precisely a constructive augmenting-path argument, which on a finite weighted graph
terminates because the set of achievable fluxes is a polytope with rational vertices
whenever the areas are rational. A general max-flow--min-cut theorem would convert every
entropy inequality proved by surface recombination into a statement about threads --- that
is, about \emph{where the entanglement lives}.

\begin{conjecture}[Tensor-network trees]
For every geometry $G$ there is a weighted tree $T$ whose leaves are the cells of $G$ and
whose induced leaf metric is exactly the emergent distance; moreover $T$ can be taken to be
the Gomory--Hu tree of $G$, with at most $|V|-1$ internal edges.
\end{conjecture}
The emergent distance is an ultrametric and $0$-hyperbolic, and finite ultrametric spaces
are exactly the leaf metrics of weighted rooted trees; the capacity hierarchy at varying
scales already produces the laminar family of clusters such a tree must have. This would
formalise the folklore that holographic states are tensor-network states: the emergent bulk
is literally a tree of contractions, computable from two-point mutual informations alone.

\begin{conjecture}[Sharp cross-section law]
In every geometry without hidden bulk cells, $E(A,B)$ equals the maximum over bipartitions
of the one-sided mutual information; in particular $I(A:B)\le 2E(A,B)$ is saturated if and
only if every minimal $A$--$B$ separating surface is homologous to $A\cup B$, i.e.\ iff the
bulk between $A$ and $B$ is a single throat.
\end{conjecture}
The proof of the cross-section bound loses exactly one inequality --- the comparison of the
two halves of the minimal $A\cup B$ surface with the true minimal surfaces of $A$ and of
$B$ --- and controlling that step is precisely a homology condition.

A fourth direction, that coarse-graining is a metric contraction, is settled above; what
remains is quantitative: bound the jump $\cpc_{\pi_*w}-\cpc_w$ in terms of the total area
of the fibre-splitting surfaces destroyed by $\pi$. A fifth is dynamics: everything here is
kinematics on a fixed slice, and the natural next object is a sequence of geometries with
an entropy production law, together with the question of whether the induced motion of the
emergent ultrametric space obeys a discrete analogue of the Einstein equations.

\section{Conclusion}

Starting from nothing but a finite weighted graph and a minimisation principle, we obtained
a metric space whose distances are exponentials of minus the entanglement, whose curvature
is as negative as it can be, whose connectivity is exactly the positivity of mutual
information, whose bridges obey monogamy, whose entanglement can be transported as a
conserved flow, and which contracts functorially under coarse-graining. Two entangled cells
really are joined by a bridge; the bridge really is wider when they are more entangled; and
severing the entanglement really does place them at maximal distance. ER $=$ EPR, in this
arena, is not a slogan but a theorem --- several of them.

\end{document}

"""
Emergent Spacetime from Quantum Entanglement
============================================

Numerical demonstrations of the combinatorial ER = EPR theory.

A *geometry* on n cells is a symmetric, nonnegative matrix w of "areas".
A *region* is a subset of cells, encoded as a bitmask.  Its area is the total
weight of the walls separating it from its complement:

    area(f) = sum_{x in f} sum_{y not in f} w[x][y]

A *holographic model* additionally marks a set of boundary cells.  The entropy
of a boundary region A is the minimal area over all regions agreeing with A on
the boundary (the discrete Ryu-Takayanagi prescription), and the mutual
information is I(A:B) = S(A) + S(B) - S(A u B).

The *throat capacity* E(A,B) is the minimal area over all regions containing A
and missing B -- the cross-section of the Einstein-Rosen bridge joining them.
The *emergent distance* is d(u,v) = exp(-E({u},{v})).

Everything is computed by exhaustive enumeration over the 2^n regions, which is
exact and fast for the small examples used here.

Run with:  python3 demo.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import math
import random
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Matrix = List[List[float]]
Region = int  # bitmask over cells


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core combinatorics
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def make_geometry(n: int, edges: Dict[Tuple[int, int], float]) -> Matrix:
    """Build a symmetric nonnegative area matrix from a dict of edge weights."""
    w: Matrix = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for (x, y), val in edges.items():
        if val < 0.0:
            raise ValueError("areas must be nonnegative")
        w[x][y] = float(val)
        w[y][x] = float(val)
    return w


def in_region(f: Region, x: int) -> bool:
    """Is cell x inside region f?"""
    return (f >> x) & 1 == 1


def region_of(cells: Iterable[int]) -> Region:
    """Bitmask of a collection of cells."""
    f = 0
    for x in cells:
        f |= 1 << x
    return f


def area(w: Matrix, f: Region) -> float:
    """Area of the surface bounding the region f (the cut weight)."""
    n = len(w)
    total = 0.0
    for x in range(n):
        if not in_region(f, x):
            continue
        for y in range(n):
            if not in_region(f, y):
                total += w[x][y]
    return total


def all_regions(n: int) -> Iterable[Region]:
    """Every one of the 2^n regions."""
    return range(1 << n)


def entropy(w: Matrix, boundary: Region, a: Region) -> float:
    """Ryu-Takayanagi entropy: minimal area over regions agreeing with A on the boundary."""
    n = len(w)
    best = math.inf
    for f in all_regions(n):
        if (f & boundary) == (a & boundary):
            best = min(best, area(w, f))
    return best


def mutual_information(w: Matrix, boundary: Region, a: Region, b: Region) -> float:
    """I(A:B) = S(A) + S(B) - S(A u B)."""
    return (entropy(w, boundary, a)
            + entropy(w, boundary, b)
            - entropy(w, boundary, a | b))


def throat(w: Matrix, a: Region, b: Region) -> float:
    """Throat capacity E(A,B): minimal area over regions containing A and missing B."""
    n = len(w)
    best = math.inf
    for f in all_regions(n):
        if (f & a) == a and (f & b) == 0:
            best = min(best, area(w, f))
    return 0.0 if best is math.inf else best


def cap(w: Matrix, u: int, v: int) -> float:
    """Bridge capacity between two single cells."""
    return throat(w, 1 << u, 1 << v)


def bridge_distance(w: Matrix, u: int, v: int) -> float:
    """Emergent distance d(u,v) = exp(-cap(u,v)), and 0 on the diagonal."""
    if u == v:
        return 0.0
    return math.exp(-cap(w, u, v))


def connected(w: Matrix, u: int, v: int) -> bool:
    """Is there a bulk path of positive-area edges from u to v?"""
    n = len(w)
    seen = {u}
    stack = [u]
    while stack:
        x = stack.pop()
        for y in range(n):
            if y not in seen and w[x][y] > 0.0:
                seen.add(y)
                stack.append(y)
    return v in seen


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bit threads
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def thread_divergence(flow: Matrix, x: int) -> float:
    """Net flux emanating from a cell."""
    return sum(flow[x])


def thread_value(flow: Matrix, source: Region) -> float:
    """Total flux emitted by the source region."""
    n = len(flow)
    return sum(thread_divergence(flow, x) for x in range(n) if in_region(source, x))


def is_valid_thread(flow: Matrix, w: Matrix, tol: float = 1e-9) -> bool:
    """Antisymmetric and capacity-respecting?"""
    n = len(w)
    for x in range(n):
        for y in range(n):
            if abs(flow[x][y] + flow[y][x]) > tol:
                return False
            if flow[x][y] > w[x][y] + tol:
                return False
    return True


def is_conserved(flow: Matrix, source: Region, sink: Region, tol: float = 1e-9) -> bool:
    """Divergence-free away from sources and sinks?"""
    n = len(flow)
    for v in range(n):
        if in_region(source, v) or in_region(sink, v):
            continue
        if abs(thread_divergence(flow, v)) > tol:
            return False
    return True


def max_flow(w: Matrix, s: int, t: int) -> Tuple[float, Matrix]:
    """Edmonds-Karp maximum flow on the undirected capacity graph; returns value and flow."""
    n = len(w)
    residual: Matrix = [row[:] for row in w]
    flow: Matrix = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    total = 0.0
    while True:
        parent = [-1] * n
        parent[s] = s
        queue = [s]
        while queue and parent[t] == -1:
            x = queue.pop(0)
            for y in range(n):
                if parent[y] == -1 and residual[x][y] > 1e-12:
                    parent[y] = x
                    queue.append(y)
        if parent[t] == -1:
            break
        bottleneck = math.inf
        y = t
        while y != s:
            x = parent[y]
            bottleneck = min(bottleneck, residual[x][y])
            y = x
        y = t
        while y != s:
            x = parent[y]
            residual[x][y] -= bottleneck
            residual[y][x] += bottleneck
            flow[x][y] += bottleneck
            flow[y][x] -= bottleneck
            y = x
        total += bottleneck
    return total, flow


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Coarse-graining
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def push_geometry(pi: Sequence[int], w: Matrix) -> Matrix:
    """Pushforward geometry: merge cells along pi, summing the areas between fibres."""
    m = max(pi) + 1
    out: Matrix = [[0.0] * m for _ in range(m)]
    for x in range(len(w)):
        for y in range(len(w)):
            if pi[x] != pi[y]:
                out[pi[x]][pi[y]] += w[x][y]
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reporting helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 74)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 74)


def check(label: str, ok: bool, detail: str = "") -> None:
    mark = "OK  " if ok else "FAIL"
    print(f"  [{mark}] {label}" + (f"   {detail}" if detail else ""))

def demo_elementary_wormhole() -> None:
    banner("1.  The elementary wormhole:  E = w,  I = 2w,  max-flow = min-cut")
    for wgt in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.5, 7.0):
        w = make_geometry(2, {(0, 1): wgt})
        boundary = region_of([0, 1])
        s0 = entropy(w, boundary, region_of([0]))
        info = mutual_information(w, boundary, region_of([0]), region_of([1]))
        thr = cap(w, 0, 1)
        val, flow = max_flow(w, 0, 1)
        print(f"  w = {wgt:5.2f} :  S({{0}}) = {s0:5.2f}   I(0:1) = {info:5.2f} "
              f"  E(0,1) = {thr:5.2f}   max-flow = {val:5.2f}   d(0,1) = {math.exp(-thr):6.4f}")
        check("throat equals the wall area", abs(thr - wgt) < 1e-9)
        check("mutual information is exactly twice the throat", abs(info - 2 * thr) < 1e-9)
        check("max-flow saturates min-cut", abs(val - thr) < 1e-9)
        check("flow is a legal thread configuration", is_valid_thread(flow, w))
        check("flow is conserved", is_conserved(flow, region_of([0]), region_of([1])))

# Demonstration 2: the ER = EPR sandwich on random geometries
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def random_geometry(n: int, rng: random.Random, density: float = 0.6,
                    scale: float = 3.0) -> Matrix:
    """A random symmetric nonnegative area matrix with the given edge density."""
    w: Matrix = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for x in range(n):
        for y in range(x + 1, n):
            if rng.random() < density:
                val = round(rng.uniform(0.2, scale), 2)
                w[x][y] = val
                w[y][x] = val
    return w


def demo_sandwich() -> None:
    banner("2.  The ER = EPR sandwich:  I(A:B)/2  <=  E(A,B)  <=  min(S(A), S(B))")
    rng = random.Random(20260819)
    n = 6
    boundary = (1 << n) - 1  # no hidden bulk
    worst_gap_left = math.inf
    worst_gap_right = math.inf
    trials = 40
    for _ in range(trials):
        w = random_geometry(n, rng)
        for u, v in itertools.combinations(range(n), 2):
            a, b = 1 << u, 1 << v
            info = mutual_information(w, boundary, a, b)
            thr = throat(w, a, b)
            sa = entropy(w, boundary, a)
            sb = entropy(w, boundary, b)
            assert info / 2 <= thr + 1e-9, (info, thr)
            assert thr <= min(sa, sb) + 1e-9, (thr, sa, sb)
            worst_gap_left = min(worst_gap_left, thr - info / 2)
            worst_gap_right = min(worst_gap_right, min(sa, sb) - thr)
            # bridge detection
            assert (thr > 1e-9) == connected(w, u, v)
    print(f"  {trials} random 6-cell geometries, all {trials * 15} cell pairs tested.")
    check("I(A:B)/2 <= E(A,B) always", True,
          f"tightest slack {worst_gap_left:.3f}")
    check("E(A,B) <= min(S(A), S(B)) always", True,
          f"tightest slack {worst_gap_right:.3f}")
    check("E(u,v) > 0  <=>  a bulk path joins u and v", True)

# Demonstration 3: the emergent metric is an ultrametric and 0-hyperbolic

def demo_ultrametric() -> None:
    banner("3.  The emergent distance is an ultrametric and 0-hyperbolic")
    rng = random.Random(31415)
    n = 6
    trials = 30
    max_ultra_violation = 0.0
    max_fourpoint_violation = 0.0
    max_triangle_slack = 0.0
    for _ in range(trials):
        w = random_geometry(n, rng)
        d = [[bridge_distance(w, u, v) for v in range(n)] for u in range(n)]
        for u, v, z in itertools.product(range(n), repeat=3):
            max_ultra_violation = max(max_ultra_violation,
                                      d[u][z] - max(d[u][v], d[v][z]))
            max_triangle_slack = max(max_triangle_slack,
                                     d[u][z] - (d[u][v] + d[v][z]))
        for x, y, z, t in itertools.product(range(n), repeat=4):
            lhs = d[x][y] + d[z][t]
            rhs = max(d[x][z] + d[y][t], d[x][t] + d[y][z])
            max_fourpoint_violation = max(max_fourpoint_violation, lhs - rhs)
    print(f"  {trials} random 6-cell geometries; all triples and quadruples tested.")
    check("strong triangle inequality  d(u,w) <= max(d(u,v), d(v,w))",
          max_ultra_violation <= 1e-9,
          f"max violation {max_ultra_violation:.2e}")
    check("ordinary triangle inequality", max_triangle_slack <= 1e-9,
          f"max violation {max_triangle_slack:.2e}")
    check("Gromov four-point condition with delta = 0",
          max_fourpoint_violation <= 1e-9,
          f"max violation {max_fourpoint_violation:.2e}")

    # A concrete ultrametric distance table.
    w = make_geometry(5, {(0, 1): 4.0, (1, 2): 1.0, (2, 3): 3.0, (3, 4): 3.0, (2, 4): 0.5})
    print("\n  Capacity table cap(u,v) for a 5-cell chain with a thin waist:")
    for u in range(5):
        row = "  ".join(f"{cap(w, u, v):5.2f}" for v in range(5))
        print(f"    {u}: {row}")
    print("  Emergent distances d(u,v) = exp(-cap(u,v)):")
    for u in range(5):
        row = "  ".join(f"{bridge_distance(w, u, v):5.3f}" for v in range(5))
        print(f"    {u}: {row}")
    print("  Isosceles law: of any three capacities, the two smallest coincide.")
    worst = 0.0
    for u, v, z in itertools.combinations(range(5), 3):
        trio = sorted([cap(w, u, v), cap(w, v, z), cap(w, u, z)])
        worst = max(worst, abs(trio[0] - trio[1]))
    check("every capacity triangle is isosceles at the bottom", worst < 1e-9,
          f"max discrepancy {worst:.2e}")

def demo_van_raamsdonk() -> None:
    banner("4.  Van Raamsdonk:  d(u,v) <= exp(-I(u:v)/2), and disentangling tears space")
    print("   A three-cell chain 0 - 1 - 2; we dial the entanglement of the 0-1 wall.")
    print("   wall w(0,1)   I(0:1)   E(0,1)     d(0,1)   exp(-I/2)   d(0,2)")
    for wgt in (0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0):
        w = make_geometry(3, {(0, 1): wgt, (1, 2): 2.0})
        boundary = region_of([0, 1, 2])
        info = mutual_information(w, boundary, region_of([0]), region_of([1]))
        thr = cap(w, 0, 1)
        d01 = bridge_distance(w, 0, 1)
        d02 = bridge_distance(w, 0, 2)
        print(f"     {wgt:6.2f}    {info:6.2f}   {thr:6.2f}    {d01:7.4f}    "
              f"{math.exp(-info / 2):7.4f}    {d02:7.4f}")
        assert d01 <= math.exp(-info / 2) + 1e-9
        assert (d01 < 1.0 - 1e-12) == connected(w, 0, 1)
    check("d(u,v) <= exp(-I(u:v)/2) throughout", True)
    check("d(u,v) = 1 exactly when no bridge joins u and v", True)
    print("   With w(0,1) = 0 the cell 0 is severed: d(0,1) = d(0,2) = 1, the maximum.")

def demo_monogamy() -> None:
    banner("5.  Monogamy:  maximal entanglement leaves a cell with exactly one neighbour")
    n = 4
    boundary = (1 << n) - 1  # no hidden bulk
    print("   Cell 0 is joined to 1 with area 3 and to 2 with area eps.")
    print("     eps     I(0:1)   2*S({0})   saturated?   I(0:2)")
    for eps in (1.0, 0.5, 0.1, 0.0):
        w = make_geometry(n, {(0, 1): 3.0, (0, 2): eps, (2, 3): 1.0})
        i01 = mutual_information(w, boundary, region_of([0]), region_of([1]))
        s0 = entropy(w, boundary, region_of([0]))
        i02 = mutual_information(w, boundary, region_of([0]), region_of([2]))
        sat = abs(i01 - 2 * s0) < 1e-9
        print(f"    {eps:5.2f}    {i01:6.2f}   {2 * s0:8.2f}   {str(sat):>10}   {i02:6.2f}")
        if sat:
            for z in (2, 3):
                assert abs(w[0][z]) < 1e-9
                assert abs(mutual_information(w, boundary, region_of([0]),
                                              region_of([z]))) < 1e-9
    check("saturation I(0:1) = 2 S({0}) forces every other wall at 0 to vanish", True)
    check("and forces I(0:z) = 0 for every other cell z", True)

def demo_bit_threads() -> None:
    banner("6.  Bit threads:  every conserved flow is bounded by every separating surface")
    rng = random.Random(2718)
    n = 6
    violations = 0
    saturations = 0
    trials = 25
    for _ in range(trials):
        w = random_geometry(n, rng)
        for u, v in itertools.combinations(range(n), 2):
            thr = cap(w, u, v)
            val, flow = max_flow(w, u, v)
            assert is_valid_thread(flow, w)
            assert is_conserved(flow, 1 << u, 1 << v)
            if val > thr + 1e-9:
                violations += 1
            if abs(val - thr) < 1e-9:
                saturations += 1
    total = trials * 15
    print(f"  {total} source-sink pairs on random 6-cell geometries.")
    check("weak duality: no conserved flow exceeds the throat capacity",
          violations == 0, f"{violations} violations")
    print(f"  Empirically the bound is attained in {saturations}/{total} cases "
          f"({100.0 * saturations / total:.1f}%), consistent with the conjectured")
    print("  strong duality (max-flow = min-cut in general), which is proved here only")
    print("  for the elementary one-throat wormhole.")

    print("\n  A concrete thread configuration on the path 0 - 1 - 2 with areas 4 and 2:")
    w = make_geometry(3, {(0, 1): 4.0, (1, 2): 2.0})
    val, flow = max_flow(w, 0, 2)
    for x in range(3):
        print("    flow[{}] = [{}]".format(
            x, ", ".join(f"{flow[x][y]:5.2f}" for y in range(3))))
    print(f"    value = {val:.2f},  throat capacity E(0,2) = {cap(w, 0, 2):.2f}")
    print("    Only the narrow wall of area 2 is saturated: it is the min cut.")

# Demonstration 7: renormalisation -- coarse-graining strictly contracts space
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_renormalisation() -> None:
    banner("7.  Renormalisation:  merging cells widens throats and contracts distances")
    w = make_geometry(4, {(0, 1): 5.0, (1, 2): 1.0, (2, 3): 5.0})
    pi = [0, 1, 1, 2]  # merge the two waist cells 1 and 2
    wc = push_geometry(pi, w)
    fine_cap = cap(w, 0, 3)
    coarse_cap = cap(wc, pi[0], pi[3])
    print("   Fine geometry: path 0 - 1 - 2 - 3 with areas 5, 1, 5.")
    print(f"     cap(0,3) = {fine_cap:.2f}   (the thin waist is the cheap surface)")
    print("   Coarse geometry after merging cells 1 and 2:")
    for a in range(3):
        print("     " + "  ".join(f"{wc[a][b]:5.2f}" for b in range(3)))
    print(f"     cap(pi0, pi3) = {coarse_cap:.2f}   (the waist is now invisible)")
    print(f"     d fine   = {bridge_distance(w, 0, 3):.6f}")
    print(f"     d coarse = {bridge_distance(wc, pi[0], pi[3]):.6f}")
    check("coarse-graining widens the throat", coarse_cap > fine_cap + 1e-9)
    check("coarse-graining contracts the emergent distance strictly",
          bridge_distance(wc, pi[0], pi[3]) < bridge_distance(w, 0, 3) - 1e-9)

    # The pullback identity, and 1-Lipschitzness on every pair.
    ok_pullback = True
    for sigma in all_regions(3):
        pulled = region_of([x for x in range(4) if in_region(sigma, pi[x])])
        if abs(area(wc, sigma) - area(w, pulled)) > 1e-9:
            ok_pullback = False
    check("every coarse surface pulls back to a fine surface of equal area", ok_pullback)
    ok_lip = all(bridge_distance(wc, pi[u], pi[v]) <= bridge_distance(w, u, v) + 1e-9
                 for u in range(4) for v in range(4))
    check("the merging map is 1-Lipschitz on the emergent metric", ok_lip)

    # Functoriality: merge again and compare with the composite.
    rho = [0, 0, 1]
    composite = [rho[pi[x]] for x in range(4)]
    left = push_geometry(rho, wc)
    right = push_geometry(composite, w)
    check("coarse-graining is functorial",
          all(abs(left[a][b] - right[a][b]) < 1e-9 for a in range(2) for b in range(2)))

def demo_bell_pairs() -> None:
    banner("8.  The emergent space of n Bell pairs is exactly n wormholes")
    weights = [2.0, 1.0, 0.5]
    n_pairs = len(weights)
    n = 2 * n_pairs
    edges: Dict[Tuple[int, int], float] = {}
    for i, wi in enumerate(weights):
        edges[(2 * i, 2 * i + 1)] = wi
    w = make_geometry(n, edges)
    boundary = (1 << n) - 1
    print("   Pair weights:", weights)
    print("   pair   I/2      E     min(S,S)    d inside    d across")
    for i, wi in enumerate(weights):
        u, v = 2 * i, 2 * i + 1
        info = mutual_information(w, boundary, 1 << u, 1 << v)
        thr = cap(w, u, v)
        su = entropy(w, boundary, 1 << u)
        sv = entropy(w, boundary, 1 << v)
        other = (u + 2) % n
        print(f"    {i}   {info / 2:6.2f}  {thr:6.2f}   {min(su, sv):8.2f}"
              f"    {bridge_distance(w, u, v):8.4f}  {bridge_distance(w, u, other):9.4f}")
        assert abs(info / 2 - thr) < 1e-9 and abs(thr - min(su, sv)) < 1e-9
    check("the sandwich collapses: I/2 = E = min(S,S) = w_i for every pair", True)

    r_low = max(math.exp(-wi) for wi in weights)
    r = 0.5 * (r_low + 1.0)
    print(f"\n   Clustering at scale r = {r:.4f}  (window [{r_low:.4f}, 1) )")
    clusters: List[List[int]] = []
    for x in range(n):
        placed = False
        for c in clusters:
            if bridge_distance(w, x, c[0]) <= r:
                c.append(x)
                placed = True
                break
        if not placed:
            clusters.append([x])
    print("   clusters:", clusters)
    expected = [[2 * i, 2 * i + 1] for i in range(n_pairs)]
    check("the clusters of the emergent ultrametric are exactly the Bell pairs",
          clusters == expected)
    print("   Below the window the space shatters into points; above it, everything merges.")

def demo_reconstruction() -> None:
    banner("9.  Reconstruction:  the entanglement table determines the whole geometry")
    n = 5
    boundary = (1 << n) - 1  # no hidden bulk
    w = make_geometry(n, {(0, 1): 2.0, (1, 2): 1.5, (2, 3): 0.75, (3, 4): 2.25, (0, 4): 0.5})
    table = [[0.0 if u == v else mutual_information(w, boundary, 1 << u, 1 << v)
              for v in range(n)] for u in range(n)]
    print("   Two-point mutual informations I(u:v):")
    for u in range(n):
        print("     " + "  ".join(f"{table[u][v]:5.2f}" for v in range(n)))
    # Rebuild the geometry from the table alone, using I(u:v) = 2 w(u,v).
    rebuilt = make_geometry(n, {(u, v): table[u][v] / 2.0
                                for u in range(n) for v in range(u + 1, n)})
    same_weights = all(abs(w[u][v] - rebuilt[u][v]) < 1e-9
                       for u in range(n) for v in range(n))
    same_metric = all(abs(bridge_distance(w, u, v) - bridge_distance(rebuilt, u, v)) < 1e-9
                      for u in range(n) for v in range(n))
    check("the areas are recovered as w(u,v) = I(u:v)/2", same_weights)
    check("hence the emergent metric spaces are isometric", same_metric)
    print("   Emergent distance matrix reconstructed from entanglement alone:")
    for u in range(n):
        print("     " + "  ".join(f"{bridge_distance(rebuilt, u, v):6.4f}" for v in range(n)))

demos.description: Two boundary cells joined by a single wall of area w -- the smallest possible wormhole. The demo computes the Ryu-Takayanagi entropies, the mutual information, the throat capacity and the emergent distance across a range of wall areas, and verifies that the whole ER = EPR sandwich collapses to a chain of equalities: half the mutual information, the throat capacity, the smaller mouth entropy and the maximal bit-thread value all equal w. Because every inequality of the theory is attained here, none of them can be improved, and the sharp constant 2 in the cross-section bound is exhibited concretely.
demos.code:
"""The elementary Einstein-Rosen bridge: every inequality becomes an equality.

Two boundary cells joined by a single wall of area w.  We verify that the
throat capacity equals w, that the mutual information is exactly 2w, that the
ER = EPR sandwich  I/2 <= E <= min(S,S)  collapses to a chain of equalities, and
that a single thread of value w saturates the min cut.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Matrix = List[List[float]]
Region = int


def make_geometry(n: int, edges: Dict[Tuple[int, int], float]) -> Matrix:
    """Symmetric nonnegative area matrix from a dictionary of wall areas."""
    w: Matrix = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for (x, y), val in edges.items():
        if val < 0.0:
            raise ValueError("areas must be nonnegative")
        w[x][y] = float(val)
        w[y][x] = float(val)
    return w


def in_region(f: Region, x: int) -> bool:

def demo() -> None:
    print(f"{'w':>6} {'S({0})':>8} {'I(0:1)':>8} {'E(0,1)':>8} {'d(0,1)':>9} "

    for wgt in (0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0):

demos.name: The Renormalisation Jump: How Blurring Destroys a Cheap Surface
demos.description: Coarse-grains a four-cell path with two heavy walls of area 5 and a thin waist of area 1 by merging the two waist cells. The demo verifies the pullback identity that drives the whole renormalisation flow (every coarse surface equals a fine surface of the same area), checks that the merging map is 1-Lipschitz on the emergent metric and that coarse-graining is functorial, and exhibits the strict contraction: the throat jumps from 1 to 5 and the emergent distance collapses from exp(-1) to exp(-5), because the unique cheap surface separated the merged cells.
demos.code:
"""The renormalisation group of emergent spacetime: merging cells contracts distance.

Coarse-graining pushes a geometry forward: the wall area between two clumps is
the total wall area between their members.  Every coarse surface pulls back to a
fine surface of exactly the same area, but fine surfaces that cut through a clump
have no coarse counterpart -- so throats can only widen and the emergent distance
can only shrink.  This demo verifies the pullback identity, the 1-Lipschitz
property and functoriality, and exhibits a four-cell path where the contraction
is strict: a waist of area 1 becomes invisible and the throat jumps to 5.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Matrix = List[List[float]]
Region = int


def make_geometry(n: int, edges: Dict[Tuple[int, int], float]) -> Matrix:
    """Symmetric nonnegative area matrix from a dictionary of wall areas."""
    w: Matrix = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for (x, y), val in edges.items():
        if val < 0.0:
            raise ValueError("areas must be nonnegative")
        w[x][y] = float(val)
        w[y][x] = float(val)
    return w


def in_region(f: Region, x: int) -> bool:
    """Is cell x inside the region f?"""
    return (f >> x) & 1 == 1


def region_of(cells: Iterable[int]) -> Region:
    """Bitmask of a collection of cells."""
    f = 0
    for x in cells:
        f |= 1 << x
    return f


def area(w: Matrix, f: Region) -> float:
    """Area of the surface bounding the region f."""
    n = len(w)
    return sum(w[x][y]
               for x in range(n) if in_region(f, x)
               for y in range(n) if not in_region(f, y))


def entropy(w: Matrix, boundary: Region, a: Region) -> float:
    """Ryu-Takayanagi entropy: min area over regions agreeing with A on the boundary."""
    n = len(w)
    return min(area(w, f) for f in range(1 << n)
               if (f & boundary) == (a & boundary))


def mutual_information(w: Matrix, boundary: Region, a: Region, b: Region) -> float:
    """I(A:B) = S(A) + S(B) - S(A u B)."""
    return (entropy(w, boundary, a) + entropy(w, boundary, b)
            - entropy(w, boundary, a | b))


def throat(w: Matrix, a: Region, b: Region) -> float:
    """Throat capacity: min area over regions containing A and missing B."""
    n = len(w)
    vals = [area(w, f) for f in range(1 << n) if (f & a) == a and (f & b) == 0]
    return min(vals) if vals else 0.0


def cap(w: Matrix, u: int, v: int) -> float:
    """Bridge capacity between two single cells."""
    return throat(w, 1 << u, 1 << v)


def bridge_distance(w: Matrix, u: int, v: int) -> float:
    """Emergent distance d(u,v) = exp(-cap(u,v))."""
    return 0.0 if u == v else math.exp(-cap(w, u, v))




def push_geometry(pi: Sequence[int], w: Matrix) -> Matrix:
    """Pushforward geometry: merge cells along pi, summing areas between fibres."""
    m = max(pi) + 1
    out: Matrix = [[0.0] * m for _ in range(m)]
    for x in range(len(w)):
        for y in range(len(w)):
            if pi[x] != pi[y]:
                out[pi[x]][pi[y]] += w[x][y]
    return out


def demo() -> None:
    w = make_geometry(4, {(0, 1): 5.0, (1, 2): 1.0, (2, 3): 5.0})
    pi = [0, 1, 1, 2]
    wc = push_geometry(pi, w)

    print("Fine geometry: the path 0 - 1 - 2 - 3 with wall areas 5, 1, 5.")
    print(f"  cap(0,3) = {cap(w, 0, 3):.2f}   (slice the thin waist)")
    print(f"  d(0,3)   = {bridge_distance(w, 0, 3):.6f}")
    print("Coarse geometry after merging the waist cells 1 and 2:")
    for row in wc:
        print("   " + "  ".join(f"{v:5.2f}" for v in row))
    print(f"  cap(pi0, pi3) = {cap(wc, pi[0], pi[3]):.2f}   (the waist is now internal)")
    print(f"  d(pi0, pi3)   = {bridge_distance(wc, pi[0], pi[3]):.6f}")
    print()

    ok_pull = all(
        abs(area(wc, sigma) - area(w, region_of([x for x in range(4)
                                                if in_region(sigma, pi[x])]))) < 1e-12
        for sigma in range(1 << 3))

                 for u in range(4) for v in range(4))
    rho = [0, 0, 1]
    left = push_geometry(rho, wc)
    right = push_geometry([rho[pi[x]] for x in range(4)], w)
    ok_fun = all(abs(left[a][b] - right[a][b]) < 1e-12 for a in range(2) for b in range(2))
    print(f"  every coarse surface pulls back with the same area : {ok_pull}")
    print(f"  the merging map is 1-Lipschitz                     : {ok_lip}")
    print(f"  coarse-graining is functorial                      : {ok_fun}")
    print()
    print("  The contraction is strict here because the unique cheap surface -- the one")
    print("  slicing the waist -- separated the two merged cells, so blurring destroyed it.")

algorithms.name: Throat Capacity of an Einstein-Rosen Bridge by Unconstrained Minimum Cut
algorithms.description: Computes E(A,B), the smallest area of a surface containing A and missing B -- the cross-section of the bridge joining them. Two implementations are provided. The exhaustive search enumerates all 2^n regions and returns both the value and a minimising region, costing O(2^n n^2) but supplying the explicit witness surface that the theory's proofs manipulate. The Edmonds-Karp maximum flow computes the same number in O(V E^2) time on the undirected capacity graph; the two agreeing is the computational face of duality, and by the Bridge Detection Theorem the answer is strictly positive exactly when a path of positive-area walls joins the two regions.
algorithms.pseudocode:
ALGORITHM ThroatCapacity(w, A, B)
  INPUT   w: symmetric nonnegative n x n area matrix
          A, B: disjoint regions, given as bitmasks
  OUTPUT  E(A,B) and a minimising separating region

  best <- +infinity ; witness <- empty
  for each region f in {0, 1, ..., 2^n - 1} do
      if A is not a subset of f then continue
      if f intersects B          then continue
      a <- 0
      for each x in f, for each y not in f do a <- a + w[x][y]
      if a < best then best <- a ; witness <- f
  return (best, witness)

ALGORITHM ThroatCapacityByFlow(w, s, t)          // polynomial alternative
  residual <- copy of w ; flow <- zero matrix ; total <- 0
  loop
      find a shortest residual path s -> t by breadth-first search
      if no such path exists then return (total, flow)
      b <- minimum residual capacity along the path
      for each edge (x,y) on the path do
          residual[x][y] <- residual[x][y] - b
          residual[y][x] <- residual[y][x] + b
          flow[x][y] <- flow[x][y] + b ; flow[y][x] <- flow[y][x] - b
      total <- total + b

algorithms.name: Ryu-Takayanagi Entropy and Mutual Information by Constrained Minimum Cut
algorithms.description: The entropy of a boundary region A is the minimal area over all regions agreeing with A on the boundary, hidden bulk cells being free -- the discrete Ryu-Takayanagi prescription, and equivalently an s-t minimum cut after contracting A to a source and its boundary complement to a sink. This routine performs the constrained minimisation exactly, returning the minimal surface as well as its area, derives the mutual information, and then audits the structural inequalities of the model on the computed values: subadditivity, the Araki-Lieb triangle inequality, strong subadditivity and the cross-section bound. Exhaustive cost is O(2^n n^2); the flow formulation is polynomial.
algorithms.pseudocode:
ALGORITHM Entropy(w, boundary, A)
  INPUT   w: area matrix; boundary: bitmask of boundary cells; A: boundary region
  OUTPUT  S(A) and a minimal surface for A

  best <- +infinity ; witness <- empty
  for each region f in {0, ..., 2^n - 1} do
      if (f AND boundary) != (A AND boundary) then continue   // homology constraint
      a <- area(w, f)
      if a < best then best <- a ; witness <- f
  return (best, witness)

ALGORITHM MutualInformation(w, boundary, A, B)
  return Entropy(w,boundary,A) + Entropy(w,boundary,B) - Entropy(w,boundary, A OR B)

ALGORITHM AuditInequalities(w, boundary, A, B, C)
  assert  S(A) + S(B) - S(AB)                >= 0    // subadditivity
  assert  S(AB) - |S(A) - S(B)|              >= 0    // Araki-Lieb
  assert  S(AB) + S(BC) - S(B) - S(ABC)      >= 0    // strong subadditivity
  assert  2 * Throat(A,B) - I(A:B)           >= 0    // cross-section bound

"""Ryu-Takayanagi entropy and mutual information by constrained minimum cut.

The entropy of a boundary region A is the minimal area over all regions that
agree with A on the boundary; hidden bulk cells are free.  This routine performs
the constrained minimisation exactly and derives the mutual information, then
verifies the structural inequalities of the model on the computed values:
subadditivity, Araki-Lieb, strong subadditivity and the cross-section bound.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Matrix = List[List[float]]
Region = int


def make_geometry(n: int, edges: Dict[Tuple[int, int], float]) -> Matrix:
    """Symmetric nonnegative area matrix from a dictionary of wall areas."""
    w: Matrix = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for (x, y), val in edges.items():
        if val < 0.0:
            raise ValueError("areas must be nonnegative")
        w[x][y] = float(val)
        w[y][x] = float(val)
    return w


def in_region(f: Region, x: int) -> bool:
    """Is cell x inside the region f?"""
    return (f >> x) & 1 == 1


def region_of(cells: Iterable[int]) -> Region:
    """Bitmask of a collection of cells."""
    f = 0
    for x in cells:
        f |= 1 << x
    return f


def area(w: Matrix, f: Region) -> float:
    """Area of the surface bounding the region f."""
    n = len(w)
    return sum(w[x][y]
               for x in range(n) if in_region(f, x)
               for y in range(n) if not in_region(f, y))


def entropy(w: Matrix, boundary: Region, a: Region) -> float:
    """Ryu-Takayanagi entropy: min area over regions agreeing with A on the boundary."""
    n = len(w)
    return min(area(w, f) for f in range(1 << n)
               if (f & boundary) == (a & boundary))


def mutual_information(w: Matrix, boundary: Region, a: Region, b: Region) -> float:
    """I(A:B) = S(A) + S(B) - S(A u B)."""
    return (entropy(w, boundary, a) + entropy(w, boundary, b)
            - entropy(w, boundary, a | b))


def throat(w: Matrix, a: Region, b: Region) -> float:
    """Throat capacity: min area over regions containing A and missing B."""
    n = len(w)
    vals = [area(w, f) for f in range(1 << n) if (f & a) == a and (f & b) == 0]
    return min(vals) if vals else 0.0


def cap(w: Matrix, u: int, v: int) -> float:
    """Bridge capacity between two single cells."""
    return throat(w, 1 << u, 1 << v)


def bridge_distance(w: Matrix, u: int, v: int) -> float:
    """Emergent distance d(u,v) = exp(-cap(u,v))."""
    return 0.0 if u == v else math.exp(-cap(w, u, v))




def entropy_with_witness(w: Matrix, boundary: Region, a: Region) -> Tuple[float, Region]:
    """Minimal area and a minimal surface for the boundary region A."""
    n = len(w)
    best, arg = math.inf, 0
    for f in range(1 << n):
        if (f & boundary) != (a & boundary):
            continue
        val = area(w, f)
        if val < best:
            best, arg = val, f
    return best, arg


def demo() -> None:
    # four boundary cells and one hidden bulk cell (index 4)
    n = 5
    boundary = region_of([0, 1, 2, 3])
    w = make_geometry(n, {(0, 4): 2.0, (1, 4): 2.0, (2, 4): 2.0, (3, 4): 2.0,
                          (0, 1): 1.0, (2, 3): 1.0})
    A, B, C = region_of([0]), region_of([1]), region_of([2])
    S = lambda r: entropy(w, boundary, r)

    print("  A hub geometry: four boundary cells all joined to one hidden bulk cell.")
    for r, name in [(A, "{0}"), (B, "{1}"), (A | B, "{0,1}"), (A | B | C, "{0,1,2}")]:
        val, witness = entropy_with_witness(w, boundary, r)
        print(f"    S({name:8}) = {val:5.2f}   minimal surface = "
              f"{[x for x in range(n) if in_region(witness, x)]}")
    print()
    print(f"    subadditivity      S(A)+S(B)-S(AB) = {S(A) + S(B) - S(A | B):5.2f} >= 0")
    print(f"    Araki-Lieb         S(AB)-|S(A)-S(B)| = "
          f"{S(A | B) - abs(S(A) - S(B)):5.2f} >= 0")
    ssa = S(A | B) + S(B | C) - S(B) - S(A | B | C)
    print(f"    strong subadd.     S(AB)+S(BC)-S(B)-S(ABC) = {ssa:5.2f} >= 0")
    gap = 2 * throat(w, A, B) - (S(A) + S(B) - S(A | B))
    print(f"    cross-section      2E(A,B) - I(A:B) = {gap:5.2f} >= 0")
    print("\n  Note the hidden bulk cell (index 4): the minimal surface for {0,1,2}")
    print("  swallows it, which is why S({0,1,2}) = 3.00 is cheaper than S({0,1}) = 4.00.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo()

algorithms.name: Construction of the Emergent Ultrametric and its Hierarchy of Entanglement Clusters
algorithms.description: Builds the capacity table cap(u,v) = E({u},{v}), converts it into the emergent distance d = exp(-cap), certifies the strong triangle inequality and Gromov's four-point condition with delta = 0, and extracts the laminar family of clusters at every scale. Because the distance is an ultrametric, 'within distance r' is a genuine equivalence relation at every r -- false for a general metric -- so the clusters are exact and nest perfectly, and the hierarchy is the dendrogram of a weighted tree. Naively the table costs C(n,2) minimum cuts; the Gomory-Hu inequality proved for the capacity kernel guarantees that n-1 cuts suffice. Verification of the four-point condition is O(n^4) once the table is in hand.

algorithms.name: Bit-Thread Synthesis with a Minimum-Cut Duality Certificate
algorithms.description: Constructs a maximum divergence-free, capacity-respecting flow between two cells by repeatedly augmenting along shortest residual paths (Edmonds-Karp, O(V E^2)), then audits the result against the defining properties of a bit-thread configuration: antisymmetry, the capacity bound |phi(x,y)| <= w(x,y), and conservation away from source and sink. It then checks weak duality against every separating surface -- the theorem guarantees the value never exceeds any of their areas -- and reports the gap to the tightest such surface, the throat. Zero gap is the computational signature of the conjectured strong duality, which is proved here for the elementary one-throat wormhole.
algorithms.pseudocode:
ALGORITHM BitThreads(w, s, t)
  (value, flow) <- EdmondsKarpMaxFlow(w, s, t)

  // audit: is this a legitimate bit-thread configuration?
  for all x, y do assert flow[x][y] = -flow[y][x]            // antisymmetry
  for all x, y do assert flow[x][y] <= w[x][y]               // capacity
  for all v not in {s, t} do assert sum_y flow[v][y] = 0     // conservation

  // audit: weak duality against every separating surface
  tightest <- +infinity
  for each region sigma containing s and missing t do
      assert value <= area(w, sigma)
      tightest <- min(tightest, area(w, sigma))
  return (value, flow, tightest, tightest - value)   // gap = 0 means duality is attained

algorithms.name: Functorial Coarse-Graining and the Renormalisation Contraction
algorithms.description: Implements the pushforward of a geometry along a merging map: the area between two coarse cells is the total area between their fibres. It verifies the pullback identity that drives the entire renormalisation flow -- every coarse surface equals a fine surface of exactly the same area -- and then measures the contraction of the emergent metric, confirming the merging map is 1-Lipschitz. It also checks functoriality of successive coarse-grainings and detects the rigidity case, in which a minimal surface happens to survive the merging and nothing moves at all. Building the pushforward costs O(n^2); the verification sweeps all 2^m coarse surfaces.
algorithms.pseudocode:
ALGORITHM PushGeometry(pi, w)
  m <- number of coarse cells
  wc <- zero m x m matrix
  for each fine pair (x,y) with pi[x] != pi[y] do
      wc[pi[x]][pi[y]] <- wc[pi[x]][pi[y]] + w[x][y]
  return wc                                  // diagonal stays zero: internal walls vanish

ALGORITHM VerifyContraction(pi, w)
  wc <- PushGeometry(pi, w)
  for each coarse region sigma do
      pulled <- { x : sigma contains pi[x] }
      assert area(wc, sigma) = area(w, pulled)        // the pullback identity
  for each fine pair (u,v) do
      assert cap(w, u, v) <= cap(wc, pi[u], pi[v])    // throats widen
      assert d(wc, pi[u], pi[v]) <= d(w, u, v)        // distances contract
  assert PushGeometry(rho, PushGeometry(pi, w)) = PushGeometry(rho o pi, w)   // functorial
